title: On estimating operator norm distance, with optimal trace distance estimation when one state is pure
authors: Yupan Liu, Qisheng Wang, Zhan Yu
abstract: We investigate the computational complexity of estimating the operator norm distance ${\rm T}_{\infty}(ρ_0,ρ_1)$, defined via the operator norm $\|A\|_{\infty} = σ_{\max}(A)$, given ${\rm poly}(n)$-size state-preparation circuits of $n$-qubit quantum states $ρ_0$ and $ρ_1$. We provide efficient quantum estimators for the operator norm distance whose complexity is independent of the rank (and thus the dimension) of the states:   1. When one state is pure, we establish an optimal quantum estimator using $Θ(1/ε)$ queries to the state-preparation circuits. Consequently, for constant additive error, say $ε=1/5$, our estimator runs in ${\rm poly}(n)$ time. Since the operator norm distance ${\rm T}_{\infty}(|ψ\rangle\!\langleψ|,ρ)$ is exactly half of the trace distance ${\rm T}(|ψ\rangle\!\langleψ|,ρ)$, our result also gives rank-independent query complexity for estimating both quantities, whereas the approaches due to van Apeldoorn, Cornelissen, Gily{é}n, and Nannicini (SODA 2023) and Wang and Zhang (TIT 2024) have query complexity scaling at least linearly with ${\rm rank}(ρ)$, which can be $\exp(n)$ in general.   2. For general quantum states, we also provide a quantum estimator using $\widetilde{O}(1/ε^{3/2})$ queries to the state-preparation circuits, which shows that the corresponding promise problem is ${\sf BQP}$-complete and improves the ${\sf QMA}$ upper bound sketched by Liu and Wang (ESA 2025). Together with an $Ω(1/ε)$ quantum query complexity lower bound, this leaves only square-root room for improvement.   The key intuition behind our estimators is that, when one state is pure, the pure state $|ψ\rangle$ has overlap at least $1/2$ with the top unit eigenvector of $|ψ\rangle\!\langleψ|-ρ$, reflecting a structural feature specific to the operator norm distance.
summary: This paper develops efficient quantum algorithms to estimate the operator norm distance between two quantum states. It achieves a breakthrough by providing estimators whose query complexity is independent of the state's rank, particularly when one state is pure. This significantly improves upon existing methods that scaled poorly with the dimension of the Hilbert space.
main_problem: The paper investigates the computational complexity of estimating the operator norm distance, $T_{\infty}(ho_0, ho_1)$, between two quantum states $ho_0$ and $ho_1$. The goal is to find estimators whose query complexity is independent of the state rank.
main_result: For the case where one state is pure, an optimal quantum estimator achieving $O(1/\epsilon)$ queries is provided, which is exponentially faster than prior methods dependent on state rank. For general states, a $\widetilde{O}(1/\epsilon^{3/2})$ query complexity estimator is derived.
method: The authors utilize quantum query algorithms and techniques involving phase estimation applied to the difference operator $\Delta = (ho_0 - ho_1)/2$. The analysis leverages structural properties, particularly when one state is pure, to establish 'warm starts' for the estimators.
model_or_system: The system involves $n$-qubit quantum states ($ho_0, ho_1$) prepared via polynomial-size circuits. The focus is on quantifying the distance between these states using operator norm and trace norms.
key_observables: Operator norm distance ($T_{\infty}$), Trace distance ($T$), Eigenvalues of difference operators ($\Delta$).
important_parameters: Error tolerance $\epsilon$, Number of qubits $n$, State rank/dimension (which the results aim to be independent of).
main_assumptions: The states are prepared using polynomial-size quantum circuits. The analysis relies on establishing overlap guarantees, especially when one state is pure.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first analyzing the optimal case (one pure state) to establish a rank-independent bound, then extending this to the general case for arbitrary states. The technical sections detail the application of phase estimation and error bounding techniques.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental algorithmic improvements for quantum information tasks, showing how structural properties (like purity) can lead to exponential speedups in estimating physical quantities like state distinguishability.
